comparator.name: Diergeneeskunde
comparator.sourceNotes: The official programme page defines a three-year full-time BSc and provides the complete curriculum by year and block. It also states that the first year comprises 60 EC. The 180-EC architecture is therefore recorded as three 60-EC years, retaining the named courses, the two longitudinal veterinary learning lines, the bachelor thesis and the genuine 22.5-EC elective space without inventing individual credit values that the public page does not publish. The two longitudinal lines develop throughout all three years and are represented within each year rather than double-counted as separate credits.
components: Year 1: Organisme tot weefsel; Van cel tot molecuul; Van cel tot weefsel; Van genoom tot populatie; Farmacologie en fysiologie; Infectie en afweer; Bloed en bloedvormende organen; Circulatie en respiratie; longitudinal Veterinaire professional and Veterinaire clinicus
The official page explicitly identifies 60 EC in year one and presents the veterinary learning lines as integrated throughout the bachelor.

Year 2: Digestie 1; Nieren en urinewegen; Digestie 2; Stofwisseling en endocrinologie; Voeding; Huid en huidderivaten; Neurologie, zintuigen en anesthesiologie; Adaptatie en welzijn; longitudinal Veterinaire professional and Veterinaire clinicus; 15 EC elective space
Includes the two genuine 7.5-EC elective slots published for block 4.

Year 3: Voortplanting; Veterinaire volksgezondheid; Locomotie; Epidemiologie en economie; bachelor thesis; Orgaanoverschrijdende aandoeningen; Heelkunde; longitudinal Veterinaire professional and Veterinaire clinicus; 7.5 EC elective space
Includes the genuine 7.5-EC elective slot and the compulsory individual English-language bachelor thesis.

exception.reason: Utrecht's Veterinary Medicine bachelor is a tightly integrated professional sequence in species-specific anatomy, embryology, physiology, pharmacology, infection and immunity, organ-system disease, animal nutrition, reproduction and obstetrics, veterinary public health, clinical diagnostics, anaesthesiology, surgery and animal-population epidemiology. Two longitudinal lines progressively develop veterinary clinical reasoning, practical skills and professional judgement, including practical work with living and dead animals, tissues and anatomical models. UCR offers valuable general biomedical, life-science, ecology, ethics and public-health courses, but it does not provide the species-specific veterinary science, clinical animal examination and treatment, surgery, reproduction, nutrition, animal-patient practicals or longitudinal veterinary clinician training on which the degree depends. A 24-course response would be a human-biomedical and ecology programme with animal-related context, not Veterinary Medicine.
exception.curriculumContext: The official current curriculum accounts for the complete three-year, 180-EC bachelor as three 60-EC years. Year one moves from mammalian and avian anatomy and embryology through molecular and cell biology, genetics, pharmacology, physiology, infection, immunity, haematology, circulation and respiration. Year two covers organ systems, nutrition across animal species, neurology, anaesthesiology, adaptation and welfare, plus 15 EC of open electives. Year three adds reproduction and obstetrics, veterinary public health and food safety, locomotion and clinical diagnostics, animal-population epidemiology and economics, a thesis, cross-organ disorders, surgery and 7.5 EC of open electives. Veterinaire clinicus and Veterinaire professional run through all three years; there is no named bachelor specialisation requiring route selection.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory, HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease provide a substantial general and human-biomedical base. HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health, HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics and HCBCOGN112 Neurobiology add population health, pathology, genetics and comparative-anatomy context. ENSECOL111 Introduction to Biodiversity, ENSECOL212 Ecosystems Uncovered, ENSECOL311 Marine Biology, ENSECOL312 Sustainable Farming & Innovation and GOSPHIL212 Ethics contribute ecology, animal biology, livestock systems, welfare-adjacent and animal-rights perspectives. The workbook nevertheless contains no comparative veterinary anatomy and organ-system sequence across mammal and bird species; no veterinary pharmacotherapy, diagnostics, anaesthesiology or surgery; no animal reproduction, obstetrics or species-specific nutrition; no food-production veterinary public-health training; and no practical progression with animal patients or longitudinal veterinary-clinician line. These are compulsory programme-wide gaps, not optional route differences.
